the PR's bit-exactness check lives inside the same multi-rank bench; the single-GPU unit tests, including its three new routing tests, pass on both boots

reason: The mark is a multi-node collective measurement. Its single-GPU parts pass on the integrated image with the PR's exact counts (396 GPU tests; 219 passed and 17 skipped CPU tests), on both boots.
notes: commands.txt start_utc is when the command was issued and includes any wait on /tmp/spark-lab-gpu.lock

The mark says 'SP gather bench at T>=6144', but in the PR's README the T>=6144 gain (-9% to -21%) is SPRows.project_exchange_rows; gather_mxfp8 falls back to PyNCCL above the one-shot cap (T=2048 on ring4, T=4096 on direct) and its table stops at T<=4096. Whoever runs it on sp1..sp4 should check which bench the mark means
The PR's CPU receipt prints 'Triton is installed but 0 active driver(s) found'; our no-visible-device run does not, so the PR's exact CPU container setup is unknown; the counts match
